key_insight: An interleaved 1H/13C MRS protocol at 7T successfully measured frontal-lobe glucose uptake and downstream metabolite labeling in vivo, supporting estimation of cerebral TCA-cycle flux.
clinical_relevance: This approach could become a minimally invasive way to probe brain energy metabolism in disorders linked to mitochondrial dysfunction and abnormal glucose utilization.
method: Interleaved ACE-STEAM (1H indirect 13C detection) and ISIS-DEPT (direct 13C detection) were used at 7T.
Three healthy volunteers underwent frontal-lobe MRS during [1-13C]-glucose infusion.
Time-resolved labeling of glucose, glutamate, glutamine, and glutamate+glutamine was fit with a one-compartment model to estimate VTCA.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports time-resolved spectral quantification, end-of-infusion enrichments, and Monte-Carlo uncertainty analysis, with a group-average VTCA of 0.66 ± 0.07 mol/g/min.
watch_item: Findings are based on only three young healthy volunteers, so broader clinical feasibility and reproducibility remain unproven.
paper_title: Assessment of Glucose Metabolism In Vivo in the Human Frontal Lobe Using Interleaved 1H and 13C MRS at 7T: Toward Clinical Translation
